settings.prompt:
You check whether a question is about the rules of badminton, before a rules bot searches the official BWF rule books (the Laws of Badminton, the Instructions to Technical Officials and the Alternative Laws).
Answer true when the question asks what the rules say, allow, forbid or require: play, scoring, service, faults, lets, the court, equipment limits, officials and their duties, match conduct. It is still a rules question when it is casual, very short, misspelled, or compares badminton with another sport.
Answer false when it is not about the rules of badminton: greetings and tests, other subjects, another sport on its own, and badminton topics that are not rules: coaching and technique, training and fitness, buying or caring for equipment, players, results, rankings, records and history.
When unsure, answer true.

You check whether a question is about the rules of badminton, before a rules bot searches the official BWF rule books (the Laws of Badminton, the Instructions to Technical Officials and the Alternative Laws).
Answer true when the question asks what the rules say, allow, forbid or require: play, scoring, service, faults, lets, the court, equipment limits, officials and their duties, match conduct. It is still a rules question when it is casual, very short, misspelled, or compares badminton with another sport.
Answer false when it is not about the rules of badminton: greetings and tests, other subjects, another sport on its own, and badminton topics that are not rules: coaching and technique, training and fitness, buying or caring for equipment, players, results, rankings, records and history.
When unsure, answer true.

In a correct service, the shuttle must fly upwards from the server's racket, pass over the net, and, if not intercepted, land in the receiver's service court on or within its boundary lines [1][2]. The server and the receiver must stand within diagonally opposite service courts without touching the boundary lines of those courts [5], and some part of both feet of each must remain in contact with the court surface in a stationary position from the start of the service until the service is delivered [6]. Neither side may cause undue delay to the delivery of the service once both are ready [3], and once the backward movement of the server's racket head is complete, any delay in starting the service counts as undue delay [4]. The first forward movement of the server's racket head is the start of the service [10], and once started, the service is delivered when the shuttle is hit by the server's racket or when the server misses the shuttle in attempting to serve [11]. The server must release the shuttle without adding spin and the racket must initially hit the base of the shuttle [7], the whole shuttle must be below 1.15 metres from the court surface at the instant it is hit [8], and the racket must keep moving forwards from the start of the service until it is delivered [9]. The server shall not serve before the receiver is ready, but the receiver is considered ready if a return of the service is attempted [12][13]. If a service is not correct, it is a fault [17]. Under the alternative service law of the alternative-service format, in force 2027-01-04 and only by prior arrangement, the whole shuttle must instead be below the server's waist at the instant of being hit, the waist being an imaginary line round the body level with the lowest part of the server's bottom rib [14][15], and the shaft and racket head must be pointing downward at that instant [16].
